questions.subject: Banking and Financial Awareness
questions.question_text: A domestic scheduled commercial bank has Adjusted Net Bank Credit (ANBC) of ₹2,00,000 crore and Credit Equivalent of Off-Balance Sheet Exposures (CEOBSE) of ₹2,10,000 crore for the relevant date. What is its agriculture lending target?

solution.explanation: PSL targets are computed on ANBC or CEOBSE, whichever is higher. Here CEOBSE (2,10,000) is higher. Agriculture target = 18% × 2,10,000 = ₹37,800 crore. (Total PSL target = 40% = ₹84,000 crore; SF/MF = 10% = ₹21,000 crore.)
solution.why_others_wrong: ₹36,000 crore uses ANBC (the lower base); ₹84,000 crore is the total PSL target; ₹21,000 crore is the small and marginal farmers target.

fact_checks.claim: Targets computed on ANBC or CEOBSE, whichever is higher; agriculture 18%, SF/MF 10%, total 40%

questions.subject: Banking and Financial Awareness
questions.question_text: A domestic bank's overall PSL achievement falls short of the target by 6 percentage points. Its shortfall is allocated to RIDF with NABARD. With the Bank Rate at 5.75%, at what interest rate will the bank earn on this deposit?

solution.explanation: Shortfall amounts are deposited in RIDF and similar funds at rates linked to the Bank Rate: Bank Rate − 2 for an overall shortfall below 5 percentage points, Bank Rate − 3 for 5 to below 10 points, and Bank Rate − 4 for 10 points or more. A 6-point shortfall earns 5.75 − 3 = 2.75%.
steps: Shortfall 6 pp → band '5 to below 10' → Bank Rate − 3
solution.why_others_wrong: 3.75% is the rate for a shortfall below 5 points; 1.75% is for 10 points or more; 5.75% is the Bank Rate itself.

fact_checks.claim: PSL shortfall deposits: Bank Rate minus 2 (<5 pp), minus 3 (5 to <10 pp), minus 4 (≥10 pp)
Bank Rate 5.75% after the October 7, 2026 MPC decision

questions.subject: Banking and Financial Awareness
questions.question_text: The Reserve Bank – Integrated Ombudsman Scheme, 2026 came into force on:

Within one year of receiving the RE's reply
Within 90 days of the expiry of the RE's reply period or its last communication, whichever is later

All scheduled UCBs, and non-scheduled UCBs with deposits of ₹50 crore and above

questions.subject: Banking and Financial Awareness
questions.question_text:
Consider the following statements about appeals under RB-IOS, 2026:
I. A complainant can appeal to the Appellate Authority against the rejection of a complaint.
II. A complainant may appeal against an Award within 30 days of receiving it, and the Appellate Authority may allow a further period of up to 30 days for sufficient cause.
III. A regulated entity cannot appeal against an Award passed because it failed to furnish the required information or documents.
Which of the above is/are correct?

solution.explanation: An appeal lies only against an Award, not against a settlement or a rejection, so I is wrong. The complainant may appeal within 30 days of receiving the Award, extendable by up to 30 more days, so II is right. An RE cannot appeal against an Award passed for its failure to furnish information or documents, so III is right.

No, no interest is payable on e₹ wallet balances

In cash through the lending service provider's agent

questions.question_text: What is the minimum 'cooling-off' period during which a borrower can exit a digital loan without penalty under the RBI (Digital Lending) Directions, 2025?

questions.subject: Banking and Financial Awareness
questions.question_text: The first pilot of the wholesale digital rupee (e₹-W), launched on 1 November 2022, was used for:

options.text: Payment of salaries to government employees
Settlement of secondary market transactions in government securities

steps: Use case: G-sec secondary market settlement

questions.subject: Banking and Financial Awareness
questions.question_text: Under the RBI (Digital Lending) Directions, 2025, where must data collected by digital lending apps be stored?

options.text: In India or any G20 country
On servers located in India; data processed abroad must be brought back within 24 hours

solution.explanation: REs must ensure that borrower data is stored only on servers located in India. If data is processed outside India, it must be deleted there and brought back to India within 24 hours. Data collection must be need-based and with the borrower's explicit consent.
steps: Processing abroad: bring back within 24 hours
solution.why_others_wrong: Encryption alone is not enough; RBI does not store lender data; G20 countries are not permitted locations.
solution.final_answer: Option D: On servers located in India; data processed abroad must be brought back within 24 hours

questions.subject: Banking and Financial Awareness
questions.question_text:
Consider the following statements under the RBI (Digital Lending) Directions, 2025:
I. A lending service provider (LSP) may collect its fee directly from the borrower if it is disclosed in the Key Fact Statement.
II. A regulated entity cannot increase a borrower's credit limit automatically without the borrower's explicit consent.
III. Repayments may be routed through the LSP's pool account for up to one day.
Which of the above is/are correct?

solution.explanation: Fees of LSPs are paid by the RE, not charged to the borrower, so I is wrong. Automatic increase of credit limits is prohibited without the borrower's explicit, recorded consent, so II is right. Repayments must go directly to the RE's account with no pass-through or pool account, so III is wrong.

fact_checks.claim: REs pay LSP fees directly and LSPs cannot charge borrowers; no automatic increase in credit limits without explicit consent; no pass-through or pool accounts

questions.subject: Banking and Financial Awareness
questions.question_text: A bank has disbursed ₹200 crore through a digital lending portfolio. Its LSP offers a default loss guarantee (DLG) of ₹14 crore on this portfolio. Under RBI's Digital Lending Directions, what is the maximum DLG cover the bank can accept?

solution.explanation: A DLG is an arrangement where an entity such as an LSP compensates the RE for losses due to default up to a specified percentage of the portfolio. The total DLG cover on any outstanding portfolio cannot exceed 5% of the amount disbursed out of it: 5% × 200 = ₹10 crore. So only ₹10 crore of the ₹14 crore offer can be accepted.
steps: Offer of ₹14 crore exceeds the cap
solution.why_others_wrong: ₹14 crore exceeds the cap; ₹20 crore applies 10%; ₹5 crore applies 2.5%.

fact_checks.claim: Total DLG cover on any outstanding portfolio shall not exceed five per cent of the amount disbursed out of that loan portfolio

questions.subject: Banking and Financial Awareness
questions.question_text:
Consider the following statements about the retail digital rupee (e₹):
I. e₹ is legal tender and a liability of the Reserve Bank of India.
II. e₹ can be made programmable, for example with an expiry date, geo-location or merchant category restrictions.
III. e₹ wallets can be offered only by banks; non-banks are not allowed.
Which of the above is/are correct?

solution.explanation: e₹ is the digital form of the rupee bank note, so it is legal tender and RBI's liability (I is right). Programmability with conditions such as expiry, geo-location, merchant category codes or merchant VPA is available, mainly for government and corporate use (II is right). e₹ wallets are offered by banks and non-banks (III is wrong).
solution.final_answer: Option A: I and II only

fact_checks.claim: e₹ is legal tender and a liability of RBI; programmable by expiry, geo-location, MCC, merchant VPA; e₹ wallets offered by banks and non-banks

questions.subject: Banking and Financial Awareness

questions.subject: Banking and Financial Awareness

A primary user to let a secondary user make UPI payments from the primary user's bank account within set limits
Merchants to accept UPI payments without a bank account
Friends to split a restaurant bill automatically

solution.explanation: India and Singapore launched a cross-border linkage between UPI and PayNow in 2023, letting users of both systems send and receive money using UPI IDs, mobile numbers or VPAs. questions.subject: Banking and Financial Awareness
questions.question_text: Meena has ₹3,000 in her UPI Lite wallet and wants to pay a shopkeeper ₹1,200. Which statement is correct?

options.text: She can pay ₹1,000 from UPI Lite and ₹200 must be paid in cash
She cannot pay ₹1,200 from UPI Lite; she must use regular UPI with her PIN
She can pay from UPI Lite because her balance exceeds ₹1,200
She can pay from UPI Lite after topping the wallet up to ₹5,000

solution.explanation: UPI Lite allows a maximum of ₹1,000 per transaction (wallet limit ₹5,000). A ₹1,200 payment exceeds the per-transaction limit, whatever the balance, so she must use regular UPI authenticated with her UPI PIN (she could also split the payment, but cash is not required).
solution.why_others_wrong: The balance and top-ups do not change the per-transaction limit; nothing forces part payment in cash.
solution.final_answer: Option B: She cannot pay ₹1,200 from UPI Lite; she must use regular UPI with her PIN

questions.subject: Banking and Financial Awareness
questions.question_text: How does NEFT settle transactions since it became available 24x7 on 16 December 2019?

options.text: Once at the end of each day
In 12 hourly batches on working days only

solution.explanation: NEFT is a deferred net settlement system owned and operated by RBI. Since 16 December 2019 it runs 24x7x365 in 48 half-hourly batches, the first after 00:30 and the last ending at 00:00 hours.
solution.why_others_wrong: Real-time individual settlement is RTGS; NEFT is not limited to working days or one daily batch.
solution.final_answer: Option D: In 48 half-hourly batches every day

fact_checks.claim: NEFT available 24x7 from December 16, 2019 with 48 half-hourly batches

questions.subject: Banking and Financial Awareness
questions.question_text: In NEFT, within what time must the beneficiary bank credit the beneficiary's account (or return the money) after the batch is settled?

options.text: By the end of the next working day

solution.explanation: The beneficiary bank must credit the account within two hours of settlement of the batch; otherwise it must return the funds within two hours of batch completion. Delays attract penal interest at the LAF repo rate plus 2%.
steps: NEFT credit or return: within 2 hours of batch settlement
solution.why_others_wrong: 30 minutes is the RTGS credit time; one hour is the RTGS return window; next-day credit is not allowed.

fact_checks.claim: Beneficiary to be credited within two hours of batch settlement, failing which funds returned; penal interest at LAF repo + 2%

questions.subject: Banking and Financial Awareness
questions.question_text: A person without a bank account wants to send money through NEFT by depositing cash at an NEFT-enabled branch. What is the maximum amount per transaction?

solution.explanation: NEFT can be used by persons without a bank account by depositing cash at an NEFT-enabled branch, subject to a limit of ₹50,000 per transaction (with KYC details). Otherwise RBI places no limit on NEFT amounts.
steps: Walk-in cash NEFT cap: ₹50,000 per transaction
solution.why_others_wrong: RBI sets no general NEFT limit, but the walk-in cash route is capped at ₹50,000.

fact_checks.claim: Non-account holders can remit through NEFT by depositing cash up to ₹50,000 per transaction

questions.subject: Banking and Financial Awareness
questions.question_text: A current account holder sends ₹1.5 lakh by NEFT at a branch, and a savings account holder sends ₹1.5 lakh by NEFT through internet banking. What is the maximum each bank may charge (excluding GST)?

options.text: ₹15 for the current account holder; nothing for the savings account holder
₹25 for the current account holder; nothing for the savings account holder

solution.explanation: Inward NEFT is free, and online NEFT from savings accounts is free. For other outward NEFT, banks may charge at most ₹2.50 (up to ₹10,000), ₹5 (₹10,000 to ₹1 lakh), ₹15 (₹1 lakh to ₹2 lakh) and ₹25 (above ₹2 lakh), plus GST. ₹1.5 lakh at a branch from a current account → up to ₹15; online from a savings account → nil.
steps: Branch NEFT of ₹1.5 lakh → slab ₹1–2 lakh → max ₹15
Online NEFT by savings account holder → free
solution.why_others_wrong: ₹25 applies above ₹2 lakh; online savings-account NEFT is free; branch NEFT for a current account is not automatically free.
solution.final_answer: Option B: ₹15 for the current account holder; nothing for the savings account holder

fact_checks.claim: Savings account holders pay nothing for online NEFT; outward charges capped at ₹2.50/₹5/₹15/₹25 by amount slab plus GST

questions.subject: Banking and Financial Awareness
questions.question_text: In the RTGS system, 'gross settlement' means that:

options.text: The transfer amount includes charges and taxes
Each transaction is settled individually, without netting against other transactions
Only transactions above ₹1 crore are settled
Transactions are added up and settled once a day

solution.explanation: In RTGS, funds are transferred continuously on a real-time basis and each transaction is settled individually (gross), not netted. Settlement takes place in the books of RBI, which makes it final and irrevocable.
solution.why_others_wrong: Batch/net settlement describes NEFT; RTGS's minimum is ₹2 lakh, not ₹1 crore; 'gross' is unrelated to charges.
solution.final_answer: Option B: Each transaction is settled individually, without netting against other transactions

fact_checks.claim: RTGS is continuous, transaction-by-transaction (gross) settlement in real time in the books of RBI

questions.subject: Banking and Financial Awareness
questions.question_text: Within how much time must the beneficiary bank credit the beneficiary's account after receiving an RTGS fund transfer message?

solution.explanation: The beneficiary bank must credit the beneficiary's account within 30 minutes of receiving the RTGS message. If it cannot, it must return the funds within one hour of receipt or before the end of the RTGS business day, whichever is earlier.
steps: If not possible: return within 1 hour
solution.why_others_wrong: Two hours is the NEFT timeline; one hour is the return window, not the credit window.

fact_checks.claim: The beneficiary bank must credit the beneficiary's account within 30 minutes of receiving the funds transfer message

questions.subject: Banking and Financial Awareness
questions.question_text: The Unique Transaction Reference (UTR) number that identifies each RTGS transaction is:

solution.explanation: Every RTGS transaction carries a 22-character Unique Transaction Reference (UTR) number. The IFSC, by contrast, is an 11-character code identifying the bank branch.
solution.why_others_wrong: IFSC has 11 characters and identifies a branch, not a transaction; 12 and 16 digits are other formats.

fact_checks.claim: Unique Transaction Reference (UTR) number is a 22-character code that uniquely identifies an RTGS transaction

questions.subject: Banking and Financial Awareness
questions.question_text: A customer wants to send three separate payments of ₹1.5 lakh, ₹3 lakh and ₹7 lakh through RTGS. Which statement is correct?

options.text: The ₹1.5 lakh payment cannot go through RTGS; the other two must be free because RTGS is 24x7
All three can go through RTGS and each can be charged up to ₹50 plus tax
The ₹1.5 lakh payment cannot go through RTGS; outward charges on the other two can be at most ₹75 plus tax
All three can go through RTGS; total charges can be at most ₹75 plus tax

solution.explanation: RTGS has a minimum of ₹2 lakh, so ₹1.5 lakh must use NEFT or IMPS. Outward RTGS charges are capped at ₹25 for ₹2–5 lakh and ₹50 above ₹5 lakh (excluding tax); inward RTGS is free. So the ₹3 lakh and ₹7 lakh payments can cost at most 25 + 50 = ₹75 plus tax.
solution.why_others_wrong: The ₹1.5 lakh payment is below the minimum; 24x7 availability does not make outward RTGS free; the ₹50 cap applies only above ₹5 lakh.
solution.final_answer: Option C: The ₹1.5 lakh payment cannot go through RTGS; outward charges on the other two can be at most ₹75 plus tax

fact_checks.claim: RTGS minimum ₹2,00,000; outward charges up to ₹25 (₹2-5 lakh) and ₹50 (above ₹5 lakh) excluding tax; inward free

questions.subject: Banking and Financial Awareness
questions.question_text: Immediate Payment Service (IMPS), an instant 24x7 interbank fund transfer service, is operated by:

solution.explanation: IMPS is operated by NPCI. It was publicly launched on 22 November 2010 and offers instant 24x7 interbank transfers through mobile, internet banking, ATMs, branches and other channels. NEFT and RTGS, by contrast, are owned and operated by RBI.
solution.why_others_wrong: RBI runs NEFT and RTGS; CCIL settles money market and G-sec trades; SBI is a bank, not a system operator.
solution.final_answer: Option A: National Payments Corporation of India (NPCI)

fact_checks.claim: IMPS is NPCI's instant 24x7 interbank electronic fund transfer service, publicly launched on 22 November 2010

questions.subject: Banking and Financial Awareness

questions.question_text: On a Sunday night, a customer wants to transfer ₹6 lakh to another bank account so that the beneficiary is credited almost immediately. Which payment system is suitable?

solution.concept: Choosing between IMPS, NEFT and RTGS

IMPS is instant but capped at ₹5 lakh per transaction. NEFT is 24x7 but settles in half-hourly batches with credit within two hours. Cheques take longer and are not cleared on a Sunday night.

questions.subject: Banking and Financial Awareness

questions.subject: Banking and Financial Awareness
questions.question_text: How are transactions authenticated in the Aadhaar Enabled Payment System (AePS)?

Through a one-time password sent to e-mail

questions.subject: Banking and Financial Awareness
questions.question_text: Which of the following activities is a payments bank NOT permitted to undertake?

options.text: Acting as a Business Correspondent of another bank
Accepting savings and current account deposits

questions.subject: Banking and Financial Awareness
questions.question_text: Under RBI's Guidelines for Licensing of Payments Banks (November 2014), what minimum share of its demand deposit balances was a payments bank required to invest in SLR-eligible government securities or Treasury Bills of up to one year?

solution.explanation: Since payments banks cannot lend, the 2014 licensing guidelines required them to invest at least 75% of their demand deposit balances in SLR-eligible government securities or T-bills with maturity up to one year, and allowed at most 25% in current and time deposits with other scheduled commercial banks.
solution.why_others_wrong: 25% is the maximum in bank deposits; 50% and 100% are not the prescribed figures.

questions.subject: Banking and Financial Awareness
questions.question_text: A customer of a payments bank has a balance of ₹1.8 lakh and receives a credit of ₹50,000 during the day. What must the payments bank ensure?

options.text: It can keep ₹2.3 lakh, because the limit applies only to savings accounts opened after 2021
It must reject the ₹50,000 credit, because the balance can never exceed ₹2 lakh even during the day
It must convert the excess into a fixed deposit with the payments bank
Not more than ₹2 lakh remains at the end of the day; the excess may be swept to a partner bank account with the customer's prior consent

solution.explanation: The ₹2 lakh limit applies to the balance at the end of the day, not to intraday credits. 1.8 + 0.5 = ₹2.3 lakh, so ₹30,000 cannot stay overnight. A payments bank may act as a BC of another bank and, with the customer's prior written consent, sweep the excess into the customer's account with that bank. Payments banks cannot accept term deposits, so a fixed deposit is not possible.
steps: End-of-day balance would be ₹2.3 lakh > ₹2 lakh
Excess ₹30,000 must leave by end of day
Route: sweep to partner bank with prior consent
solution.why_others_wrong: The cap is an end-of-day limit, applies to all individual customers, and payments banks cannot take fixed deposits.

Issued at a discount and redeemed at face value
Issued at face value and pay half-yearly interest
Issued at a premium and redeemed at a discount

solution.explanation: T-bills are zero-coupon short-term instruments of the Government of India, issued in 91-day, 182-day and 364-day tenors. They pay no interest; the investor's return is the difference between the discounted issue price and the face value received at maturity.

questions.subtopic: Instruments: T-bills, CP, CD, call money
questions.question_text: A 91-day Treasury Bill with a face value of ₹100 is bought at ₹98.50 and held to maturity. What is the annualised yield (approx.), using a 365-day year?

solution.explanation: Return = face value − price = ₹1.50 over 91 days on an investment of ₹98.50. Yield = (1.50 ÷ 98.50) × (365 ÷ 91) × 100 ≈ 6.11%. Dividing by the face value instead of the price gives the discount rate (≈ 6.02%), which understates the investor's yield.
solution.why_others_wrong: 1.52% is not annualised; 6.02% divides by face value (discount rate); 6.25% has no basis.

fact_checks.claim: T-bills are issued at a discount and redeemed at face value; 91-day tenor
